objective: Measured bounded synthetic-only baseline/Ridge/XGBoost comparison on disjoint scenario groups and chronological splits

splits.groups: train stable/rising/falling; validation seasonal/sparse; test abrupt/missing/coverage_change; robustness damped_cycle
splits.time: train labels available before 2018; validation issues 2018-2019, labels before 2020; test/robustness issues 2020+
splits.related_variants: Role and skill share each group; no family/source group crosses a split
splits.preprocessing: All ten full candidate fits use training families only; validation selects alpha/depth; no held-out refit

checks.command: synthetic_market_experiment.py prepare/run with exact code and dataset SHA-256
checks.result: 12 fits including two pilot fits; eight artifact exports; no observed hash changes; frozen selection before test metrics

artifacts: Eight baseline/model .joblib files plus synthetic metadata retained under ignored ml/artifacts/session-b/synthetic-lab/v1/models; hashes and training-label lineage in synthetic-results.v1.json
limitations: Assumed fictional worlds; no independent real demand accuracy
Training metrics are resubstitution, not holdout evidence
Validation families differ from training and test; no repeated test-driven tuning
RSS is process high-water memory including imports; not per-fit allocation
No calibrated uncertainty, real augmentation benefit or real forecast activation
The abrupt level shift begins in 2018: final test measures a sustained unseen regime, not the immediate transition. Coverage changes in 2017: history never bridges its denominator epochs.
Sparse zeros are evaluated in validation, not final test; test zero_targets is zero.
Seasonal wins validation but persistence has lower final-test MAE; no winner was reselected on that test.
Seeds/formulas are fixed assumed worlds; different-family performance is simulation robustness only.
next_eligible: SY3 exact replay, isolated-artifact runtime checks, reproducible bounded RunPod specification and model/data card
